title: 6. Market Intermediaries Regulated by SEBI (Often Asked)

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Under Section 12 of the SEBI Act, 1992, no intermediary can buy, sell, or deal in securities without obtaining a certificate of registration from SEBI.
Key primary market intermediaries include Merchant Bankers, Underwriters, Registrar and Share Transfer Agents (RTA), and Bankers to an Issue.
Secondary market intermediaries prominently feature Stock Brokers, Sub-brokers, Clearing Members, and Depository Participants (DPs).
Institutional and advisory intermediaries such as Credit Rating Agencies, Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs), Portfolio Managers, and Investment Advisers operate under explicit SEBI regulations.
SEBI enforces Code of Conduct, capital adequacy norms, and periodic inspections to ensure market integrity and safeguard investor interests.

blocks.content: No intermediary shall buy, sell or deal in securities except under, and in accordance with, the conditions of a certificate of registration obtained from the Board.

items: Section 12 of the SEBI Act, 1992 governs the mandatory registration requirement for all market intermediaries.
Questions frequently test the distinction between Merchant Bankers (issue management) and Portfolio Managers (discretionary/non-discretionary fund management).
Depositories (NSDL & CDSL) act as custodians of electronic securities, while investors interact directly with Depository Participants (DPs).
